messages.subject: Fishers Exact test or Logistics regression test and treatment statement
parts:
I have two questions that the vignette does not cover very clearly.

If I am comparing 1 control sample to say two or more test samples will the software always force a Logistics regression analysis (I guess using the pool() function will change it to Fishers).

When defining which samples/files are control and treatment does it matter in which order they are loaded or in the read statement or treatment statement.

For example does read have to be treatment first and control second like that below:
 myobj = read(file.list, sample.id = list("treatment1", "treatment2", "control1"),

Then are the treatments always 1 followed by the control being 0.
 treatment = c(1,1,0),

Thanks

Dave

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Fishers Exact test or Logistics regression test and treatment statement
parts:
On Wed, Feb 19, 2014 at 7:36 PM, <dklink...@gmail.com> wrote:
I have two questions that the vignette does not cover very clearly.

If I am comparing 1 control sample to say two or more test samples will the software always force a Logistics regression analysis (I guess using the pool() function will change it to Fishers).
pool function will pool the replicates together, and in your case you will have a new data set with one treatment and one control.

When defining which samples/files are control and treatment does it matter in which order they are loaded or in the read statement or treatment statement.

For example does read have to be treatment first and control second like that below:
 myobj = read(file.list, sample.id = list("treatment1", "treatment2", "control1"),

Then are the treatments always 1 followed by the control being 0.
 treatment = c(1,1,0),

The sample order should match the treatment vector order, meaning that files that are treatment should have 1s and the files that are control should have 0s in corresponding locations of the treatment vector. That's the most important thing. The internal code in calculateDiffMeth() subsets the methylBase object based on the treatment vector to create a treatment and control group.
